speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger; to begin our evaluation, have you noticed any recent trauma or injury to that area?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That sounds like a significant injury from the jersey pull. Did the finger deform into a "knuckle-like" shape, and are you having trouble extending it? Also, is there a visible "sister joint" (a swollen joint further up or down the finger)?

Based on the mechanism of injury (jersey pull) and your age, I suspect a "gamekeeper's thumb" equivalent or a complex joint injury. Did you hear a distinct "pop" or "snap" at the moment of impact, and is the swelling located at the base of the finger (MCP joint) rather than the tip?

text: RESULTS: X-ray of the Right Hand: No bone fractures or dislocations visible. Soft tissue swelling noted around the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Trigger Finger (Stenosing Tenosynovitis of the Flexor Digitorum Profundus), likely caused by the acute trauma and subsequent inflammation from the jersey pull incident.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
